summary: Iteration 8 checked the follow-up fixes from iteration 7. Backend: 9 of 9 new tests passed in test_iteration8_followups.py, and 28 of 28 iteration-7 security tests passed (rate-limit class skipped). /api/team returns only active members, and its count matches the active users. Pending and rejected users are excluded, and an approved user appears. /api/users returns is_owner as a boolean (true only for the owner). An upload of 20MB+10 bytes returns 413, and exactly 20MB is accepted. Code review: _run_overdue_reminders filters both the managers' CC list and the issue owner with ACTIVE. Frontend: on the Team page the owner row shows owner-badge with no remove X and a disabled role select. The self row has no remove X and a disabled select. The engineer row keeps the X and an editable select. The pending newbie shows Approve/Decline. The issue owner select lists only the 3 active members (newbie not listed). Assistant: a 429 on a new chat shows the server detail ('Too many requests, please wait a minute and try again') in the bubble and a toast. After the 60s window, the next message POSTs /ai/chat with 200 and creates a fresh session (no 404). While streaming, the session and delete buttons are disabled and the cursor is default. The pending user sees the waiting-for-approval screen on a deep link. Dashboard smoke test OK. 2 LLM calls used. Cron not triggered.

minor.issue: The API still accepts a pending or rejected user as owner_id. It returned 200 with owner 'QA Newbie' while that user was pending. The UI no longer offers these users, and the cron skips non-active owners, so the impact is low. Fix: add ACTIVE to the _owner_name lookup, which returns 404 for a non-active member.

issues: The disabled session title and delete buttons keep opacity 1, so they look the same as enabled ones (only the cursor changes). New conversation is visibly dimmed; apply the same disabled style to .session buttons.

Error bubble copy reads 'Sorry, Too many requests, please wait a minute and try again. Please try again.' It has a capital T after 'Sorry,' and says 'try again' twice. Show the detail as is, or lowercase it and drop the suffix.
The disabled role select for the owner and self rows looks identical to an editable one. Add a disabled style (muted, not-allowed cursor).
The Follow-up due field uses the browser's native date input (mm/dd/yyyy) rather than a styled date picker (carried over).

action_items: Optional: filter _owner_name by ACTIVE so the API rejects pending or rejected owners.
Optional: add a visible disabled style to assistant session/delete buttons and to Team role selects.
Optional: tidy the assistant error bubble copy (duplicated 'try again', capital T).
critical_code_review_comments: file.read(MAX_FILE+1) caps the in-memory read. Starlette still spools the full multipart body to a temp file before the handler runs, so a body-size limit at the ingress/proxy would be needed to stop very large uploads early.
When owner_id points to a rejected or pending user, the cron sets owner=None and still sends the issue to the active managers, which is good. But issue.owner still shows that person's name in the UI.
Assistant: the failed exchange from a 429 stays in the local messages list when the next message starts a new session. Display only; the server stores only the new pair.
seed_data_creation: Created and deleted the TEST_It8 Project (files and one TEST_owner issue inside). 1 chat session was created and deleted via the UI. qa.newbie was left pending; the engineer is active; owner and manager are unchanged.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run with: export REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=...; pytest -n0 tests/test_iteration8_followups.py (pytest.ini adds xdist, so use -n0 to see prints). To get a 429 on AI without LLM calls in the browser, call fetch /api/ai/draft-report with body {} 12 times using window.Clerk.session.getToken().
